sessions.title: Distinguish motion meaning, directionality and setting out

steps.title: Walking and travelling by vehicle
steps.body: идти́ — to go, walk. е́хать — to go by vehicle, ride. The first describes movement on foot; the second movement by vehicle. These are different means of moving, not an aspect pair.

steps.title: Directionality is separate from aspect
steps.body: The table places идти́ in the unidirectional column: motion in one direction. Its other column is multidirectional, covering repeated, return or different-direction movement according to context. These directionality labels are not English verb meanings. The basic unprefixed forms in these columns are imperfective; unidirectional does not itself mean perfective or arrival.

steps.title: Carrying, leading and transporting
steps.body: нести́ — to carry. вести́ — to lead. везти́ — to convey, transport. Carrying on foot, leading someone and transporting by vehicle are distinct meanings. For нести́ choose to carry. A question about its meaning is different from a question about directionality.

steps.title: Setting out does not assert arrival
steps.body: Он пошёл к другу. — he set off toward a friend. The perfective prefixed verb presents the beginning of the journey; it does not say that he arrived. Он шёл к другу. — He went to a friend's place. This retained English rendering accompanies an imperfective form describing motion toward the friend; the Russian form alone does not specify how long he was on the way. The distractor he was already on the way for a long time adds duration that is not supplied, and he refused to go contradicts the setting-out sentence.

steps.title: Read the path and only the displayed clause
steps.body: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца — The boy stepped back from the stranger. The verb and the phrase after it express movement away from the stranger. There is no additional relative clause in this displayed sentence. Они у́летят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Мяч залетел на крышу дома. — The ball flew onto the roof of the house. These are different subjects and paths. The prefix contributes to the motion meaning, while the accompanying phrases identify the path and time; do not substitute a translation of a different example.

steps.title: Interpret directionality in a whole example
steps.body: Мы идём в библиотеку. — We are headed to the library. Птицы летят на юг. — The birds are flying south. These supplied contexts show Motion in progress in one direction (imperfective). Ребёнок ходит шесть месяцев. — The child has been walking for six months. This is General walking ability (imperfective). Мы ходили по городу весь день. — We walked around the city all day. This is Movement in various directions (imperfective). Directionality is a property of the whole supplied use, not an English lexical gloss or an automatic claim that the traveller arrived. The basic unprefixed pairs are imperfective.

steps.title: Distinguish repeated trips and a completed return
steps.body: Она ходит в супермаркет каждую неделю. — She goes to the supermarket every week. This is Repeated trips (imperfective). В прошлом году я ездил в Россию. — I went to Russia (and returned) last year. In the retained supplied context this is One completed round trip in the past (imperfective). The past round-trip interpretation includes a return; the unprefixed form nevertheless remains imperfective. A choice saying “The form is perfective because this trip is completed.” makes an incorrect aspect inference for these forms. Do not equate a destination with unidirectionality or event completion with perfective aspect. Prefixed setting-out and path examples require their separately taught meanings.
